recipes.name: Grilled Swordfish Steaks with Cucumber Sauce

steps.text: Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat, and lightly oil the grate.

Stir the cucumber, sour cream, lemon juice, and lemon zest in a small bowl until combined. Season to taste with salt, and refrigerate until ready to serve. Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Stir in the onion and garlic; cook and stir until the onion has softened and turned translucent, about 5 minutes. Pour in the chili sauce, vinegar, and Worcestershire sauce. Bring to a simmer and cook 5 minutes to blend the flavors. Season with black pepper, and remove from the heat.

Brush the swordfish steaks on all sides with the 2 teaspoons of olive oil. Cook on the preheated grill until the fish is no longer translucent in the center, and easily flakes with a fork, about 3 minutes per side. Baste with the chili sauce while grilling. Serve the swordfish with lemon slices and the cucumber sauce.

raw_recipe.headline: Grilled Swordfish Steaks with Cucumber Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This wonderful, tangy sauce really compliments the flavor of grilled swordfish steaks. Serve with the cucumber sauce, and the combination of flavors are wonderful.

review.reviewBody: Keni turned me on to this tonight, and I'm glad she did. I was skeptical because I enjoy swordfish as is, with just some lemon and s&p. But, I have to say, I was pleasantly surprised!! I loved the flavors of the cucumber sauce and the bbq coated swordfish. The only thing I did different, and only because I did not have an onion, was that I used a shallot instead. I will be posting pics on my page tonight. Great recipe, awesome flavor, and it does not overpower that delicious swordfish flavor. Thanks Cyndi! (and keni, for the suggestion!)

Wonderful Recipe, Did tweak the marinade for our swordfish to our taste tonight. Followed the recipe for the cucumber sauce and it was perfect with the meaty fish!

For my marinade I used olive oil, and sesame oil, minced onion and garlic. Added Lemon Thyme, Herbes de Provence, a dash of Lemon Pepper seasoning, onion powder and salt and pepper. Grilled for 4 minutes, then turned 45 degrees to enhance grill marks and cooked 2 minutes longer. Flipped and cooked another 2-3 minutes, covered with foil while I was getting the rest of our meal finished. Served this with a Zucchini and Corn Medley and it was a perfect summer meal.

If I've had swordfish before, I do not remember it. I made this as written and it turned out pretty good. Grill time was spot on. I used an English cucumber and chose to leave the peel on for added color. After tasting the cucumber sauce I felt it need more so I gave it a few good shakes of lemon pepper. It complimented the fish perfectly but as written it made double the amount you need. Same with the chili sauce. The chili sauce was good but I felt like it masked the flavor of the fish. Overall a good recipe but one that needs some tweaks if I were to make again.

Excellent I used chili sauce with ginger. It was especially good because of the way we got the sword fish. My friend Alex ripped it out of a 5 meter long sharks mouth as he was gorging on it. True story. But that's how we do it in New Zealand.

Keni turned me on to this tonight, and I'm glad she did. I was skeptical because I enjoy swordfish as is, with just some lemon and s&p. But, I have to say, I was pleasantly surprised!! I loved the flavors of the cucumber sauce and the bbq coated swordfish. The only thing I did different, and only because I did not have an onion, was that I used a shallot instead. I will be posting pics on my page tonight. Great recipe, awesome flavor, and it does not overpower that delicious swordfish flavor. Thanks Cyndi! (and keni, for the suggestion!)

This was so good. My tomato chili sauce was kind of winged as I created the bbq sauce, but I kept to the ingredient list and it came out smashing! We occasionally grill swordfish and I am often underwhelmed, but this took it over the top! Thank You!
Delicious. The grilling sauce and the cucumber sauce was wonderful worth making. I will make it again this way
Made just as the recipe said and WOW! Super Yum! Thanks for the wonderful and tasty recipe!
3 1/2 stars without the cucumber mix. I enjoyed the cucumber mix, but I didn't find it complemented swordfish.

I have wanted to make this for so long! I was in the fish market here in Naples and noticed they had beautiful swordfish steaks, so I picked up a few. I made this as written with the exception of adding a touch of honey to the chili sauce blend. My husband is not a cuke fan, so I served his cucumber sauce in a small cup on his plate to try. He used it all and finished the entire steak (it was a good size)! I'd say that sums it up!! I enjoyed it, too! Thanks Cyndi!!

This was really good and easy to prepare. I was hoping for more spice but I guess the chili sauce I had wasn't enough. Next time I will add heat. 
Served with roasted potatoes in a spicy aioli sauce which went well with the cooling cucumber sauce.
I added garlic powder, but overall great sauce!
I tried this recipe and I though it was ok but nothing to write home about. the flavors too me did not mesh well together. over all disappointed.
I love this dish. I like spicy food so I used a thai pepper and garlic chili sauce and it was great.
